lessons.title: Recalling experience with ~던가

cards.explanation: Original practice for the HTSK Lesson 117 focus. Use the official Unit 5 page for the full explanation.

cards.translation: Did I bring my student card that day?

lessons.meaning: ~던가 is used to recall, question or check a past experience or memory.
lessons.when_to_use: Use it when the speaker is trying to remember whether or how something happened, often in a conversational question.
lessons.how_to_build: Attach the appropriate past or descriptive form before ~던가 and follow the tense and speech-level examples from HTSK.
examples: 내가 이 책을 읽었던가?
Did I read this book?
이 과자가 비싸던가?
Is this candy expensive?
파리를 죽였던가?
Did I kill the fly?
이 옷을 빨았던가?
Did I wash these clothes?
lessons.source_note: The guide is a concise paraphrase of the official HTSK lesson; the examples are separate sentences taken from that lesson page, not from the SRS cards.

cards.translation: I saw it rain yesterday
cards.explanation: Original practice for the HTSK Lesson 118 focus. Use the official Unit 5 page for the full explanation.
cards.source_sentence: 어제 비가 오더라

cards.translation: I saw that it had rained yesterday

cards.source_sentence: 어제 비가 왔더라

cards.explanation: Original practice for the HTSK Lesson 118 focus. Use the official Unit 5 page for the full explanation.
cards.source_sentence: 그 병원에서 진료를 받으면 다른 데보다 비싸더라

cards.prompt: 그 선생님이 수업을 할 때 열정이 ___

cards.prompt: 그 차고에 여러 가지 물건이 가득 쌓여 ___

cards.source_sentence: 그 차고에 여러 가지 물건이 가득 쌓여 있더라

lessons.meaning: ~더라 reports a fact or situation that the speaker personally experienced, noticed or discovered.
lessons.when_to_use: Use it when telling someone about an observed or experienced fact, often with a feeling of realization.
lessons.how_to_build: Attach ~더라 to the relevant predicate using the forms in HTSK; the ending itself carries the speaker's firsthand perspective.
examples: 가방이 무겁더라
From my own experience, I realized that the bag is heavy
이민호는 정말 멋지더라
Minho Lee is very stylish (from what I experienced)
한국말을 배우는 게 힘들더라
I realized that learning Korean is hard
문제는 컴퓨터더라
From my own experience, I realized that the problem is the computer
lessons.source_note: The guide is a concise paraphrase of the official HTSK lesson; the examples are separate sentences taken from that lesson page, not from the SRS cards.

lessons.title: Change or result with ~더니
lessons.explanation: Original practice for the HTSK Lesson 119 focus. Use the official Unit 5 page for the full explanation.

cards.explanation: Original practice for the HTSK Lesson 119 focus. Use the official Unit 5 page for the full explanation.
cards.source_sentence: 논술문제를 열심히 썼더니 손이 아파요

cards.prompt: 몸이 아파서 마사지를 ___ 몸이 더 이상 아프지 않았어요
cards.translation: Because my body was sore, I received a massage, and because of that my body is not sore anymore
cards.explanation: Original practice for the HTSK Lesson 119 focus. Use the official Unit 5 page for the full explanation.
cards.source_sentence: 몸이 아파서 마사지를 받았더니 몸이 더 이상 아프지 않았어요

cards.translation: I went into the warm water, and because of that I started to fall asleep
cards.explanation: Original practice for the HTSK Lesson 119 focus. Use the official Unit 5 page for the full explanation.
cards.source_sentence: 따뜻한 물에 들어갔더니 잠이 오기 시작했어요

cards.translation: I thought really hard, and because of that I thought of the answer
cards.explanation: Original practice for the HTSK Lesson 119 focus. Use the official Unit 5 page for the full explanation.
cards.source_sentence: 제가 곰곰이 생각했더니 정답이 생각 났어요

cards.translation: I walked all day, and because of that I am very tired
cards.explanation: Original practice for the HTSK Lesson 119 focus. Use the official Unit 5 page for the full explanation.
cards.source_sentence: 하루 종일 걸었더니 너무 피곤해요

lessons.meaning: ~더니 links a past observation with a later change, result or contrast.
lessons.when_to_use: Use it when the speaker observed one situation and then saw what happened afterward, especially an unexpected result.
lessons.how_to_build: Attach ~더니 to the first clause and conjugate the following clause normally; follow the subject and tense restrictions described by HTSK.
examples: 의자 등받이에 허리를 대고 오랜 시간 앉았더니 허리가 아파요
I sat with my back against the chair for a long time and now it hurts
장난으로 녀석이라는 말을 자주 쓰기 시작했더니 실수로 동생에게 녀석이라고 불렀어요
I started using 녀석 as a joke and then accidentally called my younger sibling that
슬기가 체육시간에 너무 많이 달리더니 다음 수업을 들을 수 없었어요
Seulgi ran so much in P.E. that she could not attend the next class
lessons.source_note: The guide is a concise paraphrase of the official HTSK lesson; the examples are separate sentences taken from that lesson page, not from the SRS cards.

lessons.title: Surprise with ~다니
lessons.explanation: Original practice for the HTSK Lesson 120 focus. Use the official Unit 5 page for the full explanation.

cards.translation: I’m glad that your dad is coming as well
cards.explanation: Original practice for the HTSK Lesson 120 focus. Use the official Unit 5 page for the full explanation.

cards.translation: It’s too bad that your parents are getting a divorce

cards.translation: I can’t believe Seulgi is going to graduate school
cards.explanation: Original practice for the HTSK Lesson 120 focus. Use the official Unit 5 page for the full explanation.
cards.source_sentence: 슬기가 대학원에 가다니 믿을 수 없어

cards.prompt: 해양 생물이 점점 사라지고 ___ 믿을 수가 없다

cards.explanation: Original practice for the HTSK Lesson 120 focus. Use the official Unit 5 page for the full explanation.
cards.source_sentence: 해양 생물이 점점 사라지고 있다니 믿을 수가 없다

cards.prompt: 부모님의 허락도 없이 쌍꺼풀 수술을 ___ 정말 실망이다
cards.translation: I’m disappointed that you would get double eyelid surgery without your parents’ permission
cards.explanation: Original practice for the HTSK Lesson 120 focus. Use the official Unit 5 page for the full explanation.
cards.source_sentence: 부모님의 허락도 없이 쌍꺼풀 수술을 하다니 정말 실망이다

lessons.meaning: ~다니 is a quoted or exclaimed form used to react with surprise, disbelief or strong feeling toward information.
lessons.when_to_use: Use it when the speaker is reacting to what was said or what has happened, often with an emotional tone.
lessons.how_to_build: Form the relevant quotation before 니: verb, adjective, noun and past forms use the contractions explained in HTSK.
examples: 놀이터에 있는 그네가 망가졌다니 믿을 수 없다
I can’t believe that the swing in the playground broke
우리가 만든 드라마의 시청률이 떨어졌다니 너무 실망스러워요
I’m very disappointed that the ratings for the drama we made dropped
동네 내과에 갔더니 대학 병원 내과에 가라고 하다니 점점 걱정이 되기 시작했다
I went to a local clinic, and they told me to go to a university hospital, so I started to get more worried
너의 부모님이 이혼하신다니 안됐다
It’s too bad that your parents will get a divorce (now that I have heard that your parents will get a divorce, it is too bad)
lessons.source_note: The guide is a concise paraphrase of the official HTSK lesson; the examples are separate sentences taken from that lesson page, not from the SRS cards.

lessons.title: As time passes with ~다 보면
lessons.explanation: Original practice for the HTSK Lesson 121 focus. Use the official Unit 5 page for the full explanation.

cards.translation: If you do construction on the road again without purpose the citizens will protest
cards.explanation: Original practice for the HTSK Lesson 121 focus. Use the official Unit 5 page for the full explanation.
cards.source_sentence: 쓸데없이 차도를 다시 만드는 공사를 매년 하다 보면 시민들이 항의해요

cards.prompt: 혼자서 ___ 부모님을 보고 싶은 것은 당연한 게 아니에요?
cards.translation: If you (continue to) live alone, isn’t it obvious that you will want to see (miss) your parents?
cards.explanation: Original practice for the HTSK Lesson 121 focus. Use the official Unit 5 page for the full explanation.
cards.source_sentence: 혼자서 살다 보면 부모님을 보고 싶은 것은 당연한 게 아니에요?

cards.translation: If I keep memorizing new words, I gradually get confused
cards.explanation: Original practice for the HTSK Lesson 121 focus. Use the official Unit 5 page for the full explanation.
cards.source_sentence: 새로운 단어를 계속 외우다 보면 점점 헷갈려요

lessons.meaning: ~다 보면 means if one continues doing something or as time passes while doing it, a result may occur.
lessons.when_to_use: Use it for a result that emerges naturally through repeated or continued experience.
lessons.how_to_build: Attach the appropriate quoted/plain form + 보면 to the first clause and conjugate the result clause normally.
examples: 네가 그렇게 열심히 일하다 보면 승진하게 될 거야
If you continue to work hard like that, you will likely be promoted
이 길을 계속 따라가다 보면 찾고 있는 시장이 나타날 거예요
If you keep following this road, the market you are looking for will appear
고아원에서 봉사를 하다 보면 감사하는 태도로 살아야겠다는 생각이 들어요
After volunteering repeatedly at an orphanage, I realized that I must live with a thankful attitude
바쁘게 살다 보면 가끔 중요한 일을 잊어버려요
If you continue to live a busy life, sometimes you will forget important things
lessons.source_note: The guide is a concise paraphrase of the official HTSK lesson; the examples are separate sentences taken from that lesson page, not from the SRS cards.

lessons.title: Unexpected result with ~다 보니
lessons.explanation: Original practice for the HTSK Lesson 122 focus. Use the official Unit 5 page for the full explanation.

cards.translation: While I was studying, it became 12:00
cards.explanation: Original practice for the HTSK Lesson 122 focus. Use the official Unit 5 page for the full explanation.
cards.source_sentence: 제가 공부하다 보니 12시가 되었어요

cards.translation: While I was exercising, I realized that my arm was sore
cards.explanation: Original practice for the HTSK Lesson 122 focus. Use the official Unit 5 page for the full explanation.
cards.source_sentence: 운동하다 보니까 팔이 아팠어요

cards.prompt: 화분을 ___ 누런 싹이 싹튼 식물이 몇 개 보였어요

cards.explanation: Original practice for the HTSK Lesson 122 focus. Use the official Unit 5 page for the full explanation.
cards.source_sentence: 화분을 청소하다 보니 누런 싹이 싹튼 식물이 몇 개 보였어요

cards.prompt: ___ 로마 제국까지 공부해야 한다는 것을 느꼈어요
cards.translation: While studying about the country of Greece, I felt that I should also study up to the Roman Empire
cards.explanation: Original practice for the HTSK Lesson 122 focus. Use the official Unit 5 page for the full explanation.
cards.source_sentence: 그리스라는 나라를 공부하다 보니 로마 제국까지 공부해야 한다는 것을 느꼈어요

cards.prompt: 셋째를 ___ 우리 아이 모두를 평등하게 돌보지 않을 뿐만 아니라 큰애에 매우 소홀하다는 것을 깨달았어요
cards.translation: While looking after my third child, I realized that not only was I not looking after all of my children equally, but also that I was really neglecting my oldest one
cards.explanation: Original practice for the HTSK Lesson 122 focus. Use the official Unit 5 page for the full explanation.
cards.source_sentence: 셋째를 돌보다 보니 우리 아이 모두를 평등하게 돌보지 않을 뿐만 아니라 큰애에 매우 소홀하다는 것을 깨달았어요

lessons.meaning: ~다 보니 means that after doing something or as a result of continuing, the speaker discovered an often unexpected result.
lessons.when_to_use: Use it when the result becomes apparent through experience rather than being planned in advance.
lessons.how_to_build: Attach the relevant verb form before 보니, following the contraction and tense patterns shown by HTSK.
examples: 길거리를 걷다 보니 물방울이 느껴져서 비가 온다는 것을 알았어요
While walking down the road, I felt some water droplets, and knew it was raining
그 사람이랑 얘기하다 보니까 세계 서열 1위의 부자일수도 있다고 생각했어요
While talking to that person, I thought it could be possible that she is one of the richest people in the world
아버지와 논쟁하다 보니 이제부터 아버지 말에 복종해야 한다는 것을 깨달았어요
While arguing with my father, I realized that I should have obeyed him (his words) starting from yesterday
그리스라는 나라를 공부하다보니 로마 제국까지 공부해야 한다는 것을 느꼈어요
While studying about the country of Greece, I felt that I should also study up to the Roman Empire
lessons.source_note: The guide is a concise paraphrase of the official HTSK lesson; the examples are separate sentences taken from that lesson page, not from the SRS cards.

lessons.explanation: Original practice for the HTSK Lesson 123 focus. Use the official Unit 5 page for the full explanation.

cards.prompt: 에너지를 발산하려고 운동을 ___ 삶의 원동력이 생겼어요

cards.explanation: Original practice for the HTSK Lesson 123 focus. Use the official Unit 5 page for the full explanation.
cards.source_sentence: 에너지를 발산하려고 운동을 해 보니까 삶의 원동력이 생겼어요

cards.prompt: 유가의 가격을 강제적으로 ___ 시장에 문제가 생겼어요
cards.translation: After having tried forcing the price of oil down, I now realize that it created problems in the market
cards.explanation: Original practice for the HTSK Lesson 123 focus. Use the official Unit 5 page for the full explanation.
cards.source_sentence: 유가의 가격을 강제적으로 낮춰 보니까 시장에 문제가 생겼어요

cards.translation: After having tried running my business conscientiously, customers just started coming in naturally
cards.explanation: Original practice for the HTSK Lesson 123 focus. Use the official Unit 5 page for the full explanation.
cards.source_sentence: 양심적으로 장사를 해 보니까 자연스럽게 손님이 늘었어요

cards.prompt: 연애를 ___ 남자들을 더 잘 이해하게 되었다
cards.translation: Now that I have tried/attempted having a boyfriend, I became able to understand men better
cards.explanation: Original practice for the HTSK Lesson 123 focus. Use the official Unit 5 page for the full explanation.
cards.source_sentence: 연애를 한번 해 보니까 남자들을 더 잘 이해하게 되었다

cards.prompt: 공연을 진행할 때 더 활발하게 ___ 사람들이 더 환호했어요
cards.translation: When I ran the performance, when we marched more actively people cheered more
cards.explanation: Original practice for the HTSK Lesson 123 focus. Use the official Unit 5 page for the full explanation.
cards.source_sentence: 공연을 진행할 때 더 활발하게 행진해 보니까 사람들이 더 환호했어요

lessons.meaning: ~아/어 보니까 means after trying or experiencing something, I found or realized that.
lessons.when_to_use: Use it when direct experience leads to a discovery or changed understanding.
lessons.how_to_build: Attach ~아/어 보니까 to the verb stem with the normal vowel rule; the following clause states what was discovered.
examples: 한번 머리를 염색해 보니까 염색이 생각만큼 간단하지 않다는 걸 알게 됐다
Now that I have tried/attempted to dye my hair, I realize/can assert that doing so is not as simple as one thinks
과학 공부를 해 보니까 많은 과학 서적 내용이 검증이 필요하다는 걸 알게 됐다
Having studied science, I now know that the material in science books require a lot of verification
그 회사가 획기적으로 건물 디자인을 구축해 보니까 사람들이 반응이 더 좋았어요
After that company constructed a groundbreaking design for their building, they realized people’s reactions were better
저자가 다른 작가에 좌우되지 않고 책을 더 잘 쓰기 위해 자신에 더 집중해 보니까 더 진지하게 작품을 쓸 수 있게 됐어요
In order to write his own book well, the writer realized that not allowing himself to be influenced by other works allowed him to write his piece more seriously.
lessons.source_note: The guide is a concise paraphrase of the official HTSK lesson; the examples are separate sentences taken from that lesson page, not from the SRS cards.

cards.explanation: Original practice for the HTSK Lesson 124 focus. Use the official Unit 5 page for the full explanation.

cards.translation: That teacher deserves an award

cards.prompt: 그 의사는 많은 사람의 목숨을 살려서 칭찬을 ___

cards.source_sentence: 그 의사는 많은 사람의 목숨을 살려서 칭찬을 많이 받을 만해요

cards.translation: Our grandfather deserves a lot of respect for fighting in the Korean war

cards.source_sentence: 우리 할아버지는 한국전쟁에서 싸우셨으므로 존경을 받을 만해요

cards.translation: Do you know a worthwhile place to eat?

cards.source_sentence: 먹을 만한 식당을 알아요?

lessons.meaning: ~ㄹ/을 만하다 means worth doing or sufficiently possible, and 가치가 있다 expresses that something has value.
lessons.when_to_use: Use it to evaluate whether an action or experience is worth the time, effort or risk.
lessons.how_to_build: Attach ~ㄹ 만하다 after a vowel or ㄹ stem and ~을 만하다 after another consonant; use 가치가 있다 in the noun construction from HTSK.
examples: 외국어를 배울 만한 가치가 있어요
It is worth learning a foreign language

lessons.meaning: ~ㄴ/는다니까 is a contracted quoted form used to insist that the speaker has already said something, often with frustration or emphasis.
lessons.when_to_use: Use it in a response when repeating information that the listener should already know; HTSK warns that it can sound rude or sassy.
lessons.how_to_build: Start from the plain quoted form + 고 하니까 and contract it: present verbs, past, future, adjectives, nouns and commands have the separate forms shown by HTSK.
examples: 반이상 정답을 맞추면 합격으로 간주한다니까
I already said that if you get more than half correct then it is considered a pass
이런 빵은 너무 두껍다니까
I told you that this kind of bread is too thick
그 사람은 보면 볼수록 예쁘다니까
I told you that the more you look at that person, the more pretty she is
이게 내 것이라니까!
(Ugh, I already said that) this is mine
